text:
sam: Quick perf check for the v2.3 rollout — canary rev 2026-04-15-rc3. Smallbatch run shows p95 ~12% up vs baseline. Need a fast decision: hold, rollback, or proceed with mitigations?

deploy-bot: Deployment canary started for service=runtime-realtime rev=2026-04-15-rc3 (canary=5%).

nathan: Can you paste the exact bench command and the numbers you saw?

sam: ```
./bench/latency --model rdx-2-small --seq 1024 --concurrency 8 --batch-size 4
baseline (prev rev 2026-04-12-rc2): p95=210ms p99=480ms
current canary (rc3): p95=235ms p99=510ms
GPU util (avg per-GPU): 78% -> 87%
errors: 0, OOMs: 0
notes: observed spike during prefix handling phase
```

mia: Staging can be noisy. Was this reproduced on a dedicated node (same GPU type)? If not, can you run the same bench on dedicated-qa? Also try --no-prefetch and --no-batching to isolate.

patrick: Requesting a quick profile: pprof + torch cuda sync timings, and a kernel breakdown. If attention kernel time increased we need to know if it's model/seq-related vs batching behavior.

sam: I ran a short kernel profile earlier — found ~30% increase in time spent in torch_cuda_synchronize and 18% regression in matmul kernel for this workload. Uploading trimmed flamegraph to s3://redwood-temp/perf/1771234567/flame-small.svg (will post full later).

anna: Per rollout policy, our auto-hold thresholds: p95 increase >10% OR GPU util >85% OR error-rate delta >0.5% -> hold. This matches two triggers (p95 and gpu). My recommendation: hold the canary and rollback to rc2 while we triage.

eng-oncall: I agree with @anna. I'll trigger a conservative rollback now unless someone objects in the next 5m. If we want to keep canary for extra telemetry we should pin traffic to 0% and keep the infra for profiling.

sam: No objection. We'll keep one canary instance running (0% traffic) for debug dumps. Rolling back sounds best.

eng-oncall: /deploy rollback service=runtime-realtime target=2026-04-12-rc2 scope=canary

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated: runtime-realtime -> rev 2026-04-12-rc2. Canary traffic set to 0% while prev stable is restored. Reason: p95 delta >10%.

nathan: Action items: 1) @sam run focused microbench on dedicated-qa with seq=512 and seq=1024, with and without batching; 2) @mia run pprof with perf-record + flamegraph on the held canary instance; 3) @patrick check kernel selector logs and recent kernel changes (two patches landed this week). I'll open an issue to track triage.

mia: I'll take the pprof job. Prefer perf-record --call-graph dwarf + python stack sampling, then produce flamegraphs and annotate hotspots. Ping me with the canary node id.

sam: Will run the microbench now and upload results to s3://redwood-temp/perf/1771234567/results.json. Also capturing nvprof traces. ETA 25m.

nathan: I'll create perf issue: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RINF-3221 (perf/regression, priority=P1, assignees: sam, mia, patrick). Include links to bench logs + flamegraph.

adeena: :thumbsup: (react)

deploy-bot: Release-gate: canary held. Gate reason: p95 increase 11.9% (threshold 10%).

sam: Thanks. We'll triage and aim for a follow-up decision in this thread: rollback confirmed, triage in progress, plan to either fix & re-roll or rollforward behind perf mitigations.

patrick: If we prove it's a kernel regress, we may be able to hotfix kernel selection or fallback to previous kernel until proper patch lands. I'll look into safe knob toggles.

eng-oncall: Closing rollout window and notifying SRE oncall for infra snapshot retention. Next update in ~1h or sooner with bench + profile links.

sam: Filed the issue and uploaded initial bench logs: s3://redwood-temp/perf/1771234567/results.json. Will update in place.

mia: Got the node id from @eng-oncall. Starting perf record now.

patrick: Adding note: check quantization path as well — there was a recent opt that touched int8 kernel path.

sam: Acknowledged.

nathan: Thanks everyone. Good call on holding.
